categories.main_business_segments: Chubu Electric Power operates three main business segments: 'Miraiz' (retail electricity and gas sales and related services), 'Power Grid' (electricity transmission and distribution network services), and 'JERA' (fuel upstream and procurement, power generation, and wholesale electricity and gas sales). The group also engages in related construction, manufacturing, and real estate businesses, as well as overseas energy operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Core technologies include large-scale power generation (hydroelectric, nuclear, thermal, and renewables), advanced grid management and transmission systems, and energy trading. The company is investing in decarbonization technologies such as hydrogen and ammonia co-firing, renewable energy integration (including offshore wind), and digital transformation (DX) for grid and demand management. R&D focuses on safety improvements for nuclear power, expansion of renewables, and next-generation network technologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are residential, commercial, and industrial electricity and gas users, mainly in the Chubu region of Japan. The company also serves other utilities and participates in wholesale markets, with growing activities in overseas energy markets and real estate development. Key markets include energy consumers in Japan and select international regions where the group has investments or partnerships.
categories.geographic_coverage: The core geographic focus is the Chubu region of Japan (including Aichi, Gifu, Mie, Nagano, and Shizuoka prefectures), but the company also operates nationally through JERA and has overseas investments in Europe (notably the Netherlands and Germany), Southeast Asia (Vietnam), and North America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chubu Electric Power operates across the entire energy value chain: upstream (fuel procurement via JERA), midstream (power generation and grid operation), and downstream (retail electricity and gas sales, customer services). The company also participates in infrastructure construction, maintenance, and real estate, positioning itself as a vertically integrated utility with diversified interests.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include ensuring stable energy supply, accelerating decarbonization (with a goal of net-zero CO2 emissions by 2050), expanding renewable energy capacity, and promoting digital and green transformation (GX/DX). R&D is directed at safety enhancements for nuclear power, renewable energy integration, hydrogen/ammonia technologies, and innovative customer services. The company is also focused on business model transformation to deliver new value-added services and address regional and societal challenges.
categories.revenue_model: The primary revenue model is based on electricity and gas sales to end-users (both regulated and competitive markets), network usage fees, and wholesale transactions. Additional revenue streams come from construction, maintenance, real estate leasing and sales, and overseas energy investments. The company also receives government subsidies for certain energy transition initiatives.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other major Japanese electric utilities (such as TEPCO, Kansai Electric, and Kyushu Electric), new entrants in the deregulated retail energy market, and global energy companies in overseas ventures. Chubu Electric Power is one of Japan's largest utilities, with a strong regional base and a growing presence in renewables and international energy markets, positioning itself as a leader in the energy transition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was approximately 3.67 trillion yen, with operating profit of 242 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 202 billion yen. The company has over 22,000 employees and total assets exceeding 7.1 trillion yen. While profitability declined from the previous year due to market and cost factors, the company maintains a large scale and is targeting stable profit growth and improved capital efficiency through business diversification and innovation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chubu Electric Power emphasizes reliable and stable energy supply, competitive pricing, and a strong commitment to decarbonization and sustainability. The company differentiates itself through integrated energy solutions, advanced grid management, customer-centric service innovation, and leadership in the adoption of new technologies (such as hydrogen and renewables). Its value proposition also includes contributing to regional development and addressing social challenges through infrastructure and community-focused initiatives.
